rows.name: TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL
rows.who_sets: The Nix lint shell and the Nix `lefthook` wrapper (`flake.nix`).
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` turns it on. Any other text counts as off.
rows.default: Unset: off. The hook commands try `ci/.venv/bin/ruff` and `ci/.venv/bin/python` first, then the tools on `PATH`.
rows.effect: With `1`, the Lefthook (Git hook runner) commands `ruff-format`, `ruff-check` and `agent-guidance` run `ruff` and `python3` from `PATH` and do not look in `ci/.venv/bin`. `bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh` does the same for `python3`. A missing `ruff` or `nixfmt` then fails the hook command.
rows.notes: `flake.nix` sets `1` in the Nix lint shell (`nix develop .#lint`, `x86_64-linux` only) and in the `lefthook` wrapper of the Nix dev shell. `bin/ci/test-nix-lint-toolchain.sh` fails without `1`. Without `1`, a missing `ruff` or `nixfmt` is skipped when `CI` is unset or empty.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_CONFIG
rows.values: Path of a Perfetto config file in protobuf text format. A path that starts with `/` is used as written. Any other path is relative to the repository root.
rows.default: Unset: `tronperf` uses `perfetto/runtron.cfg` as the base config.
rows.effect: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for runtron) uses the file as its base config. `perfetto/generate-config` applies the command-line options of `tronperf` on top of it.
rows.notes: The option `--perfetto-config` overrides it. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read it. A file that `generate-config` cannot read or parse stops `tronperf` with exit status 2.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT
rows.values: Whole seconds from `1` to `30`, as 1 or 2 decimal digits. `08` means 8 seconds. Any other text stops the launcher with exit status 2.
rows.effect: Sets the longest time that `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the 2 Perfetto launchers) wait for each readiness signal. There are 3 signals: from `traced`, from `traced_probes` (the 2 Perfetto daemons) and from the `perfetto` client. The limit applies to each wait separately.
rows.notes: When a wait reaches the limit, the launcher prints an error and exits with a non-zero status. The error for a rejected value is `TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT must be an integer from 1 to 30`.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR
rows.who_sets: The Nix dev shell and the `nix run` apps `tronperf`, `wrapper`.
rows.values: Path of a directory that holds the generated Python module `perfetto_config_pb2` and the file `perfetto_schema_release.txt`.
rows.default: Unset: `generate-config` does not change the Python module search path. It imports `perfetto_config_pb2` from the existing path.
rows.effect: `perfetto/generate-config` (the script that builds the Perfetto config for the launchers `tronperf` and `wrapper`) puts the directory first on the Python module search path. It then imports `perfetto_config_pb2`.
rows.notes: `generate-config` exits with status 1 when the import fails. It also exits when `perfetto_schema_release.txt` beside the imported module is missing or does not hold `57.2`. The `nix run` apps and the Nix dev shell replace any earlier value. `perfetto/test_perfetto.py` reads the variable the same way.

rows.name: TRON_RUNTRON
rows.values: Path of a runtron executable. The text is used as the command. `tronperf` does not check it.
rows.effect: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for runtron) starts this program with `--trace traced` after the Perfetto session is ready. With the option `--gen`, it passes `--trace-gen traced` instead.
rows.notes: `perfetto/wrapper` does not read it. `tronperf` starts the Perfetto session before it runs the program. A wrong path fails only at that point.

rows.name: TRON_TP_ADDR
rows.values: `HOST:PORT` of a running `trace_processor_shell --httpd` server, for example `127.0.0.1:9001`. The text is passed unchanged to the Perfetto Python package.
rows.default: Unset: no default address. Without a trace path and without `--addr`, the script prints an error and exits with status 2.
rows.effect: When the command line has no trace path and no `--addr` option, the script connects to that trace processor server (`trace_processor_shell`, the Perfetto program that runs SQL queries on a trace). It then loads no trace file. It does not use `--bin-path` or `TRON_TP_BIN`.
rows.notes: The option `--addr` overrides it. With a trace path, the script loads the trace itself and ignores the variable.

evidence.quote: if addr is None and not args.trace:
if not addr and not args.trace:

rows.name: TRON_TP_BIN
rows.who_sets: The Nix dev shell. Outside `x86_64-linux` it sets an empty value.
rows.values: Path of an executable `trace_processor_shell` (the Perfetto program that runs SQL queries on a trace). The Python scripts expand a leading `~`.
rows.default: Unset: `analyze_kv_duration` exits with status 2. The 2 `tron_*.py` scripts do the same without `--bin-path`. `rinzler-capture.sh` skips its trace summary.
rows.effect: The Python scripts pass the path as `bin_path` to the Perfetto Python package to load a trace. `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh` (the capture script for a running rinzler) runs the program 4 times after a capture and prints a summary of the trace.
rows.notes: The option `--bin-path` of the 2 `tron_*.py` scripts overrides it. A path that is not an executable file makes the Python scripts exit with status 2. `rinzler-capture.sh` then skips its summary. `tron_trace_query.py` does not use it in `--addr` mode.

evidence.quote: echo "(TRON_TP_BIN unset; run inside nix develop for a capture summary)"

rows.name: TRON_TRACEFS
rows.who_sets: Nothing in TRON, except one test in `perfetto/test_perfetto.py`.
rows.values: Only the exact text `/sys/kernel/tracing` is accepted. Any other non-empty text stops the launcher with an error and exit status 2.
rows.default: Unset: the check passes. The launchers use `/sys/kernel/tracing`.
rows.effect: The variable does not select a tracefs (Linux kernel tracing file system) directory. `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the 2 Perfetto launchers) always use `/sys/kernel/tracing`. They only reject a different value.
rows.notes: The error message names `TRON_TRACEFS` and the required path.

evidence.quote: error "TRON_TRACEFS must be $DEFAULT_TRACEFS because traced_probes uses that path"

rows.name: UV
rows.who_sets: CI workflows, as `/tools/uv/<version>/uv`. A developer, to select another `uv`.
rows.values: Command name or path of `uv` (the Python package manager that the repository uses). The text is used as the command.
rows.default: Unset: `make` and the 2 `bin/ci` scripts run `uv` from `PATH`. The Python scripts try `PATH`, then `/tools/uv/uv`. Empty: `make` keeps the empty text.
rows.effect: `make` runs it for the `*-deps` targets, `python-lock` and the `gen/tokenize_py` build. `ingest/build-model.py` and `bin/extract_logits` run it to start the export scripts of `ingest/export`. CI steps run `$UV sync` to install Python environments, and 2 CI scripts run `bin/ci/benchmark_info.py` with it.
rows.notes: Empty value: the `make` recipes have no program name, and the Python and `bin/ci` scripts treat it as unset. With a non-empty `IN_NIX_SHELL`, `make` runs it only for `proxy-test-deps` and `python-lock`. `ingest/build-model.py` does not run it with a non-empty `IN_NIX_SHELL` or with `--export-with-current-python`.

rows.name: VERBOSE
rows.values: `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh`: only the exact text `true` turns it on. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh`: any non-empty text turns it on.
rows.effect: Two unrelated scripts read it. `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh` (the request generator for Perfetto captures) prints the text of each model response. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` (the Rust version check and setup script) prints its information messages.
rows.notes: In `burst-test.sh`, the option `-v` or `--verbose` sets it to `true`. CMake runs `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` at configure time and prints its output. An exported value adds the messages there. The option `-v` of `rust-toolchain.sh` also turns on shell tracing. The variable alone does not.

rows.name: WEIGHTS
rows.values: Path of model weights. `ingest/build-all.sh` passes the text unchanged as the `--default-weights` argument of `ingest/build-model.py`.
rows.default: Unset: the script passes no `--default-weights` for a model whose registry entry has no `default_weights`.
rows.effect: `ingest/build-all.sh` passes the value as `--default-weights` to `ingest/build-model.py`, for each model whose entry in the model registry (`config/models.yaml`) has no `default_weights`. `build-model.py` does not use the argument in these runs. The generated files do not change.
rows.notes: `build-model.py` uses `--default-weights` only when it adds a model configuration entry. It adds none with `--no-config`. `build-all.sh` passes `--no-config` for every model that has an architecture name. `config/model_definitions.py` gives every registry model such a name.

rows.name: WEIGHTS_ROOT
rows.who_sets: A developer, by hand. `config/test_model_definitions.py` sets it in one test.
rows.values: Path of a directory. It holds one sub-directory of model weights for each Hugging Face model ID.
rows.effect: `ingest/build-all.sh` passes `<WEIGHTS_ROOT>/<model ID>` to `ingest/build-model.py` as the model path (`-m`). A model whose directory does not exist fails with `local weights not found`.
rows.notes: A required model without a directory ends the script. An optional one is only reported. `ingest/build-model.py` does not read the variable. It has its own fixed path `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`. For a model path outside that path, it passes no `--tokenizer` argument to the export step.

evidence.quote: echo "=== $(red Error): $(blue $model) local weights not found at $local_path"

rows.name: WINDOW_MS
rows.values: Whole number of milliseconds. The script uses the text in bash arithmetic and does not validate it.
rows.effect: Sets the arrival window of `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh` (the request generator for Perfetto captures). Each request starts at a random offset from 0 milliseconds to less than this value.
rows.notes: The option `-w` or `--window-ms` overrides it. With `0`, every request starts at offset 0 milliseconds.

rows.name: pci_id
rows.values: Text of the form `vvvv:dddd`: a PCI vendor ID of 4 hex digits, a colon, and a device ID of 4 hex digits. The script passes it unquoted to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh`.
rows.default: Unset: `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` gets only the card address. It prints a warning and continues without the ID check.
rows.effect: Unless its first argument is `unbind`, `bin/bind-cards.sh` passes the value to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` for each FPGA card. That script checks for a device with this vendor and device ID at the card address, then binds the card to `vfio-pci` (the Linux driver for user-space PCI access). A mismatch stops both scripts.
rows.notes: The script takes `pci_id` from its environment and never assigns it. It prints the value in each `binding` line. The `unbind` mode does not use it. Text in another form, such as `8200:`, stops the script. Text in PCI address form replaces the card address.

evidence.quote: echo "Error: Vendor:Device ${VD} not found at ${BDF}, unable to bind device" 1>&2
echo "Warning: You did not specify a Vendor:Device (vvvv:dddd), unable to validate ${BDF}" 1>&2

rows.name: start_address
rows.values: Offset from the base address, as hexadecimal digits without the `0x` prefix. The script adds `0x` in front and uses the text in bash arithmetic without a check.
rows.default: Unset: the offset counts as 0. The first address is the base address `0x37000000000`.
rows.effect: `bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh` uses `start_address` before it assigns it. On the first pass of its loop it adds the inherited value to the base address `0x37000000000`. It writes a test pattern to that memory address with `./iotools mmio_write64` and reads it back.
rows.notes: Each later pass adds the address of the previous pass to the base address again. The script reads the address range of each line of `address_map_1.csv` into `range` and never uses it. It runs `./iotools` from the current directory.

evidence.quote: while IFS=, read -r name _ _ _ range _; do

new_terms.definition: The launcher `perfetto/tronperf`. It starts a Perfetto session and then runs runtron with tracing turned on.
The launcher `perfetto/wrapper`. It starts a Perfetto session and can signal a running process, such as rinzler, to emit trace events.
The 2 Perfetto daemons that the launchers start before the `perfetto` client.
The Perfetto program `trace_processor_shell`. It loads a trace file and runs SQL queries on it.
The Linux kernel tracing file system, mounted at `/sys/kernel/tracing`.
The Git hook runner that runs the lint commands of `lefthook.yml` before a commit.
The development environment that `nix develop .#lint` starts. It holds the pinned lint tools.
The Python package manager that the repository uses to install its pinned Python environments.
The file `config/models.yaml`. It lists the models that TRON supports.
The Linux driver that gives a user program direct access to a PCI device, such as an FPGA card.

notes: All 15 names are kept and none is dropped. Every evidence quote of the earlier rows matched its source line. Rows changed in meaning: `TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL` (a missing `ruff` also fails with `1`, the lint shell exists only on `x86_64-linux`), `TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT` (the limit is per wait, with 3 waits), `TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR` (the `nix run` apps and the dev shell replace a caller value), `TRON_TP_ADDR` (the effect has a condition), `TRON_TP_BIN` (`rinzler-capture.sh` skips its summary for a non-executable path), `UV` (the workflow steps have no fallback for an empty value, and `make` skips `uv` in most targets inside a Nix shell), `WEIGHTS` (the effect cell now states that the value changes no generated file), `WEIGHTS_ROOT` (no `--tokenizer` argument for a directory outside the fixed path of `build-model.py`), `pci_id` (a wrong ID stops both scripts). A sentence that says an empty value equals unset is removed from 10 default cells and 1 notes cell. The row format gives an `Empty:` clause only when empty differs from unset. `pci_id` and `start_address` are lower-case shell names that their scripts use and never assign first. The scripts take them from the environment. No file in the checkout sets or documents them. Evidence quotes avoid source lines that hold a bar character. For that reason the `nixfmt` test of `lefthook.yml` and the 3 range checks of `perfetto/launcher-common` have no quote. Two behaviours were confirmed outside the checkout with scratch commands: GNU Make 4.3 keeps an empty `UV` with `?=`, and bash 5.1.16 evaluates `0x` as 0.

changes.name: pci_id
changes.was: In bind mode, `bin/bind-cards.sh` passes the value to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` for each FPGA card. That script checks that a device with this vendor and device ID is at the card address before it binds the card to `vfio-pci` (the Linux driver for user-space access to a PCI device).
changes.now: Unless its first argument is `unbind`, `bin/bind-cards.sh` passes the value to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` for each FPGA card. That script checks for a device with this vendor and device ID at the card address, then binds the card to `vfio-pci` (the Linux driver for user-space PCI access). A mismatch stops both scripts.
changes.why: The row did not say what a wrong ID does. `vfio_pci_bind.sh` prints an error and exits with status 1 when the ID is not at the address (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:122-124). `bind-cards.sh` runs with `set -e` and stops at that card (bin/bind-cards.sh:3). The cell also now says what bind mode is (bin/bind-cards.sh:9, bin/bind-cards.sh:22).

changes.name: pci_id
changes.was: The script never assigns `pci_id`. The value comes from the environment. Unbind mode (first argument `unbind`) does not use it. Text in another form, such as `8200:`, stops the script with an error. Text in the form of a PCI address replaces the card address.
changes.now: The script takes `pci_id` from its environment and never assigns it. It prints the value in each `binding` line. The `unbind` mode does not use it. Text in another form, such as `8200:`, stops the script. Text in PCI address form replaces the card address.
changes.why: Added a way to see the value that the script received: `echo "binding $i $pci_id"` (bin/bind-cards.sh:26). This matters, as `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` exits unless it runs as root (bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh:64-67), and the value must be in the environment of that root process. Other sentences are shortened only.
